descriptionChirho: To verbally censure or admonish someone for wrongdoing (Hifil active); Arabic وَبَّخَ (wabbakha 'rebuke'), Korean 꾸짖다/책망하다 (kkujitda/chaemang-hada 'rebuke/reprove'), Swahili -kemea ('rebuke'), Hindi डाँटना (daantna 'scold/rebuke'). This is the core Hifil sense covering all inflections of direct verbal reproof.

To reprove with the intent of moral correction or parental discipline (Hifil with pedagogical nuance); Arabic يُؤَدِّبُ (yu'addibu 'discipline/educate') and لِلتَّأديبِ (lit-ta'dib 'for discipline'), distinct from وَبَّخَ; Swahili -adhibu ('punish'), kurekebisha ('correct'); Hindi ताड़ना (taadna 'chastisement'). Context: divine or parental correction (2 Sam 7:14, Prov 3:12).

To render a decision, judge between parties, or arbitrate a dispute (Hifil in juridical contexts); Arabic يَحْكُمُ (yahkumu 'judge') and عَيَّنَ ('ayyana in arbitral sense), Korean 판단하다 (pandanhada 'judge/decide'), Swahili -amua ('decide') and mpatanishi ('mediator'), Hindi फैसला करना/निर्णय करना (phaisla karna/nirnay karna 'make a decision'). Context: Messianic and covenant justice (Isa 2:4, 11:3, Mic 4:3).

To present arguments, reason in a legal or disputational context, prove one's case (Hifil and Nifal in forensic-rhetorical contexts); Arabic يُحَاجُّ (yuhajju 'argue/dispute') and أُبَرِّرُ (ubarriru 'justify/vindicate') and وَتُثْبِتُونَ (wa-tuthbituna 'and you prove'), Korean 항변하다 (hangbyeonhada 'plead/argue'), Swahili -jadiliana ('debate'), -tetea ('defend'), -thibitisha ('prove'). Distinct from rebuke: this is reasoned argumentation, not censure.

To appoint or designate someone for a role or task (Hifil with unique semantic shift); Arabic عَيَّنَ ('ayyana 'appoint'), Korean 정하다 (jeonghada 'determine/set'), Swahili -mchagua ('choose/select'), Hindi निर्धारित करना (nirdharit karna 'designate'). Completely distinct from all reproof/argumentation senses; likely a homonymous or highly extended sense of the root.

To be vindicated or declared innocent (Nifal passive/reflexive); Arabic تَبَرَّأَ (tabarra'a 'be acquitted/cleared'), Korean 의로워지다 (uirowojida 'become righteous'), Swahili sahihi ('correct/valid'), Hindi सही ठहराया गया (sahi thehraya gaya 'was justified'). A Nifal sense with distinct passive-juridical meaning: being shown to be in the right.

To engage in mutual contention or disputation (Hitpael reflexive/reciprocal); Arabic يَتَخَاصَمُ (yatakhaasamu 'quarrel/litigate mutually'), Korean 논쟁하다 (nonjaenghada 'debate/dispute'), Swahili -hukumiana ('judge one another'). The Hitpael stem marks reciprocal or intensive disputation, distinct from Hifil argue/contend.
